en.title: Future plans
en.goal: Express plans and intentions using 要 and 打算.

lessons.planos: Saying what you plan to do
lessons.viagem-estudo: Talking about travel and study plans

phrases.t: What are your plans for tomorrow?
In the future I want to travel to China.

dialogue.title: Talking about the future
lines: What are your plans for next week?
Do you want to go to China in the future?
Yes! I want to travel to China.

dasuan.title: 打算 (dǎsuàn) — future plans
dasuan.body: 打算 (dǎsuàn) means "to plan" or "to intend", and is followed directly by a verb — it is one of the most common ways to talk about future plans in Chinese.

yihou.title: 以后 (yǐhòu) — "after"
yihou.body: 以后 (yǐhòu) means "after" or "in the future", and comes after the time reference it relates to — the whole structure (time + 以后) works as a unit meaning "after that moment".
examples: in the future I want to travel to China

yihou.title: "Dǎsuàn" or "yào"?
yihou.body: Dǎsuàn (打算) is a more thought-out plan, with some organization. Yào (要, which you saw back in Unit 5) can express a more immediate or simple intention, "I'm going to do it". Dǎsuàn sounds a bit more formal and deliberate than yào.
examples: I want to travel to China (intention)

review.pt: No futuro eu quero viajar para a China.
review.en: In the future I want to travel to China.
review.why: word order natural alternative: 'I want to travel to China in the future'

review.pt: Quero! Eu quero viajar para a China.
review.en: Yes! I want to travel to China.
review.why: answer to 要 question; alt 'I do!'

review.pt: Dǎsuàn soa um pouco mais formal e deliberado que yào
review.en: Dǎsuàn sounds a bit more formal and deliberate than yào
